newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares closed below the day's highs on Friday, falling back in the last hour or so of trade as Wall Street relinquished some of its recent gains.

Shares here surged during the morning following third quarter results from foods and household products firm Unilever, which topped some expectations and raised some of the recent gloom about what have been seen as disappointing Dutch results.

The AEX share index closed 4.11 points higher at 592.71, down from the day's high of 596.36 but above support seen at 590. Dealers said the index looked to be on course next week to brush aside the October 21 all-time high of 597.80.

Another gain on Wall Street on Thursday, hard on the heels of Wednesday's near 100 point post-U.S. election surge, sent the Amsterdam market higher this morning with some investors said to have been squeezed after ignoring the U.S. rally yesterday.
"Some people are having to pay up for stock they could have got a guilder cheaper yesterday," one dealer said earlier.

Analysts said chart formations pointed towards another high in the AEX next week with the index seen above 600 for the first time ever. "It only looks like a matter of a few days before the AEX gets to the 600 level," said one chartist, saying today's close above 590 gave a positive signal.
"Maybe we might fall back a little at the beginning of the day on Monday if Wall Street remains negative at the close but if stocks close on Monday above 590, I'm a buyer," he added.

Unilever's 1.31 billion guilder third quarter net profit at current exchange rates, up from the previous 1.22 billion, was at the upper end of the 1.15 to 1.33 billion forecast range and dealers said this had dispelled some gloom at recent results.

"People yesterday were negative after the disappointing third quarter figures reports we've had -- only Unilever has been better than (most) expectations," said a dealer. The shares closed 16.60 guilders higher at 275.20.

Analysts said the third quarter net exceptional charge of 81 million guilders was lower than anticipated and this had also helped the shares, although profit-taking might subsequently kick on speculation of a big fourth quarter charge.
Food and drinks company BolsWessanen closed 1.10 guilders higher at 32.30, boosted by a fresh round of bid speculation, this time focusing on food group CSM as a potential predator.

A CSM spokeswoman categorically denied that the firm planned to make an offer for BolsWessanen. "This is a surprise to us. The company absolutely denies it has any plans to approach BolsWessanen," she said. BolsWessanen declined to comment.
CSM finished the day 1.90 guilders lower at 93.70, hurt by the rumours which analysts said made little commercial sense.
Unilever was by far the day's major gainer among the blue chips, followed by Royal Dutch 2.30 guilders higher at 273.30, Ahold up 1.60 guilders to 105.20 and Heineken 1.20 guilders firmer at 324.00.

Outside of these gains were relatively modest and a fair number of declines were seen, including KLM off 30 cents to 41.20 guilders and Akzo 0.70 guilders easier at 213.00 -- both after results earlier this week. -- Keiron Henderson, Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
